fields.h1: Build a Ranking Survey That Scores Every Item by Points
fields.hero_description: Build a ranking survey people answer by dragging items into order, with points per item and every ranking in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Every Ranking
fields.features_subheading: A ranking survey has two sides: the screen where people put items in order, and the readout that turns their orders into one list.
fields.feature_1:
Every rank used exactly once

Emergent writes the ranking question so each item takes its own place, with no ties. A list of 5 items comes back as 5 distinct ranks, and each rank is saved to its own column.
fields.feature_2:
Drag to reorder on a phone

Respondents press and drag each item into place, one question per screen, so a list of 6 fits a phone without sideways scrolling. Each finished order saves as soon as they tap Next.
fields.feature_3:
Points per item, added up on the dashboard

The dashboard weights each place, 5 points for first down to 1 for last on a 5-item list, and totals each item. Ask for other weights in a prompt and Emergent rebuilds the totals.
fields.feature_4:
Top picks split by customer group

Add a question such as plan type or region, and the dashboard shows first choices for each group side by side. An item that wins overall can still come second with one group.
fields.feature_5:
The final order, sent to the team

When the survey closes, the app posts the ranked list to a Slack channel or sends it by email. Each new ranking can also sync to any tool with an API, such as HubSpot or Stripe.
fields.feature_6:
Code that moves with you

Every survey Emergent builds is code. Export it to your GitHub repository on paid plans and keep the question logic, the scoring, and the dashboard in a repo you control.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams Putting a List in Order
fields.tab_content_1:
Calendar sync wins on points, 1,604 of 6,180

Glimmerbook asks 412 customers to rank 5 roadmap features. The dashboard gives 5 points for a first place down to 1 for last and totals each feature. Calendar sync leads with 1,604 points, and bulk edit is second at 1,388.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each buyer group puts a different blend first

Pinecrest Roasters sells 4 blends and asks 300 buyers to rank them, plus one question on how they buy. Among 140 subscribers, 60 put the single origin first. Among 160 first-time buyers, 72 put the house blend first, and the dashboard sets the two groups side by side.
fields.tab_content_3:
On a phone, 286 attendees drag topics into order

The Mosswood Design Summit asks 286 registered attendees to rank 6 session topics before it sets the program. Each attendee drags the topics into place on a phone, one question per screen. Accessibility audits draws 97 first-place votes, and design systems follows with 64.
fields.tab_content_4:
The final order lands in #it-planning on Friday

Halyard Freight's IT team asks 38 department heads to rank 5 project requests. When the survey closes on Friday, the app posts the final order to the #it-planning Slack channel. The laptop refresh comes first with 182 of 570 points, ahead of the VPN upgrade at 141.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Ranking Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a ranking survey with Emergent, score each item by points, and see which one people put first.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Cut the list to 5 or 6 items
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add one or two profile questions
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the decision the ranking feeds before you list a single item: which feature ships next, or which blend goes on the homepage. An item that cannot change that decision does not belong on the list. Write the rest down in plain words.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep only the items you could act on. Each item you add is one more that every respondent has to weigh against all the others, and the places in the middle of a long list carry the least signal. Five or six is plenty.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe the survey in a prompt: the items, who answers, and how many points each place earns. Emergent builds the ranking question, the respondent screens, and a dashboard that totals the points. Ask for changes the same way, in plain English.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a question or two that describe the respondent, such as plan type or how long they have been a customer. Place them after the ranking, so the list is the first thing people see and answer while their attention is fresh.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the survey to five colleagues and watch two of them rank on a phone. If anyone asks what an item means, rename it in plain words. Check that each test ranking reaches the dashboard with the points you expect.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Share the link and set a close date
fields.howto_step_6_des: Publish the survey and share the link by email or inside your product. Set a closing date before you send it, and ask Emergent to add a reminder email for anyone who has not answered after 3 days.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read points and first places together
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the points total next to the count of first places. An item that leads on both is a clear winner. An item with high points but few first places is broadly liked yet rarely anyone's favorite; weigh it against the leader before you decide.

faq_plan.q: What are ranking questions in a survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are ranking questions in a survey?

prov.original: What are ranking questions in a survey?

faq_plan.a: Ranking questions in a survey hand respondents a short list and have them compare the items against each other, putting the one they prefer most at the top and the one they prefer least at the bottom. Because no two items can share a place, the answer shows what wins when two good options compete. A ranking survey is built around one or more of these lists.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a ranking survey?
faq_plan.a: Write a prompt for Emergent's AI survey builder that lists the items, the audience, and the scoring. Emergent turns that prompt into a working survey with its own results page, and you change any part by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Can you give me an example of a ranking question in a survey?
faq_plan.ref: Can you give me an example of a ranking question in a survey?

prov.original: Can you give me an example of a ranking question in a survey?

faq_plan.a: Yes: "Rank these 5 features in the order you want them built, with 1 as the one you want most." Respondents then drag calendar sync, bulk edit, offline mode, dark mode, and custom fields into order. A coffee brand might ask buyers to rank 4 blends from favorite to least favorite.

faq_plan.q: When should I use rank order survey questions instead of rating questions?
faq_plan.a: Use rank order survey questions when you need a winner, because ranking forces a preference for one item over another. A rating question compares items on a common scale, and two items can score the same. If you only need to know whether people want an item at all, a yes no questions survey is faster than either.

faq_plan.q: What are good survey ranking questions examples for customer research?
faq_plan.a: Try these three. Ask customers to rank the reasons they chose you, from most to least important. Have them put support channels in order of how they prefer to reach you. A third lists 4 plan features by how much each would sway a decision to upgrade. Each ties the list to one decision the team can act on.

faq_plan.q: How do I analyze ranking survey questions?
faq_plan.hint: How to analyze ranking survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start with a weighted score: give first place the most points, 5 on a 5-item list, and one point less for each place after it, then add up each item. Then count first places, since an item can earn high points without being anyone's favorite. Read the middle places with care; they carry the most noise. A dashboard Emergent builds can show both counts side by side.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to finish a ranking survey?
faq_plan.a: Put the ranking first, show one question per screen, and say up front how many questions there are. A light opener can help: one of a few funny survey questions, such as ranking pizza toppings, gets people used to dragging items before the list that counts. Emergent can build the survey as one question per screen on a phone.

faq_plan.q: How many items should a ranking survey question have?
faq_plan.a: Five or six suits a phone. SurveyMonkey's help center suggests limiting ranking choices to about 5, and a Qualtrics guide suggests 6 to 10 items. Qualtrics also notes that the middle rankings are the noisiest. With 20 candidates, screen them first and write ranking questions for surveys that cover only the shortlist.

faq_plan.q: Is there a limit on how many people can answer a rank order survey?
faq_plan.a: Not on a survey Emergent builds, which has no response cap. A rank order survey sent to every customer keeps counting each answer, and the dashboard totals update as rankings come in. That lets you watch the order settle before the close date.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a poll and a ranking survey?
faq_plan.a: A poll asks for one pick; a ranking survey asks for the whole order. Use poll questions when you only need the favorite, and a survey ranking when second and third place matter too, as when you can fund 2 projects out of 5. The full order takes respondents a little longer to give.

plan.angle: The top 10 is help docs and explainers on ranking questions (how to write one, dos and don'ts, example lists) plus a few survey tools. None shows what a finished ranking survey looks like once the answers are in. This page shows the build and the readout together: weighted points per item, the top pick split by customer group, drag-to-rank on a phone, and the final order posted to the team when the survey closes, with every ranking a row in a database the team owns. The FAQ answers what a builder asks before launch: what a ranking question is, examples, how many items, how to score and read the results, and when a rating or a poll fits better.
tab_stories: Glimmerbook, a note-taking app, asks 412 customers to rank 5 roadmap features; the app scores 5 points for a first place down to 1 for last, and calendar sync leads with 1,604 of 6,180 points.

Pinecrest Roasters asks 300 buyers to rank 4 blends; 60 of 140 subscribers (43%) put the single origin first, while 72 of 160 first-time buyers (45%) put the house blend first, so the dashboard splits first choices by buyer type.
The Mosswood Design Summit asks 286 registered attendees to drag 6 session topics into order on a phone, one screen per question; accessibility audits gets 97 first-place votes.

Halyard Freight's IT team asks 38 department heads to rank 5 project requests; when the survey closes on Friday, the app posts the final order to the #it-planning Slack channel, with SSO rollout first at 182 of 570 points.

intent.evidence: Top 10 mixes tool pages (SurveyMonkey help, Jotform, OpinionX) with how-to and example guides (Qualtrics, Pollfish, SurveyPlanet); page delivers the builder, a 7-step how-to, examples ('Rank these 5 features in the order you want them built', three customer-research examples in FAQ 5), scoring and analysis ('Start with a weighted score').

specificity.evidence: Ranking-specific detail throughout: 'A list of 5 items comes back as 5 distinct ranks', '5 points for first down to 1 for last', 'Read the points total next to the count of first places'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences with verbs: 'Emergent writes the ranking question...', 'Respondents press and drag...', 'Glimmerbook asks 412 customers...', 'Pick the decision the ranking feeds...'.

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (under the cap); sentences short and varied; no blocking craft defect. Notes recorded.

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led: 'An item that cannot change that decision does not belong on the list.' 'An item that wins overall can still come second with one group.' No AI-tell vocabulary.
